meta.title: Open Office Studio — OpenAEC Foundation
meta.description: Open Office Studio: free, open source office suite for Windows, macOS and Linux. Word, Excel and PowerPoint files, notes, email and Access databases, on your own computer and without an account.

header.label: Office suite
header.title: Open Office Studio
header.tagline: All your office work on your own computer
header.desc: Documents, spreadsheets, presentations, notes, email and databases in one program. It opens and saves Word, Excel and PowerPoint files directly, without an account or cloud service.

notice.text: In development: these are development releases, not yet signed off for production work. Test with copies of your files.

features.label: Features
features.heading: Six apps in one suite
features.sub: Start with the highlights or pick a topic.

writer.title: Edit Word documents directly
writer.desc: Page view, rulers, ribbon and styles. With headers and footers, a table of contents, footnotes, comments, track changes and comparing two versions.

sheet.title: Excel files with formulas and charts
sheet.desc: Formulas, cell formatting, sorting and fill, with eleven chart types. Input like 1,5, € 1.234,50 or 26-10-2026 is recognised as a number or date.

slides.title: Create and present PowerPoint files
slides.desc: Slides, shapes, text and speaker notes, and a slideshow from the first or current slide.

notes.title: Notebooks that stay local
notes.desc: Notebooks, sections and pages, saved locally and automatically, with backups. Each section is a free canvas or a Markdown page with preview, tables and task lists.

db.title: Open Access databases without Access
db.desc: Opens MDB and ACCDB and builds an editable SQLite working copy; the original stays untouched. With tables, queries, simple forms and reports, and a compatibility report per file.

mail.title: Your email, with no party in between
mail.desc: An IMAP and SMTP client with folders, search and attachments. Office attachments open as an editable copy, and any open document can be sent as an attachment. External images stay blocked until you allow them.

layout.title: Formatting and styles
layout.desc: Style editor, lists, borders, tables, images, sections and columns.

review.title: Reviewing together
review.desc: Comments, track changes and comparing two versions.

csv.title: CSV and TSV
csv.desc: Import and export, with freeze panes, AutoSum and find and replace.

charts.title: Eleven chart types
charts.desc: Insert and edit in documents, spreadsheets and presentations.

markdown.title: Markdown
markdown.desc: Source editor with live preview, tables and task lists, plus import and export.

oauth.title: Sign in with Microsoft and Google
oauth.desc: Through OAuth2, with your own client ID. Server settings are suggested when you add an account.

vba.title: VBA in a sandbox
vba.desc: Runs only after your permission, without COM, Windows APIs or file access. Nothing starts by itself.

export.title: Export a database
export.desc: Save as SQLite, tables and queries as CSV, and source as SQL or BAS.

tabs.title: Document tabs
tabs.desc: Everything in one window; drag a tab out into its own window.

formats.title: About fifteen formats per module
formats.desc: The app itself writes DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, Markdown, HTML and PDF, among others. With LibreOffice also OpenDocument and older Office formats.

spell.title: Spell checking
spell.desc: Dutch and English with Hunspell dictionaries, suggestions and autocorrect.

recovery.title: Crash recovery
recovery.desc: Automatic recovery, recent files, print preview and light and dark themes.

download.label: Download
download.title: Download v2026.45.4
download.lead: Free and without an account. Signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux.
download.mobileNote: Open Office Studio is a desktop app. Download it on your computer.
download.appsLead: Only need one part? Every app has its own installation and its own profile.
download.note: Everything runs on your own computer. Open Office Studio collects no usage data.

whatsnew.label: New in v2026.45
whatsnew.title: Save as IFCX, better notes and tables
whatsnew.desc: The releases of week 45 bring saving as IFCX, more control over footnotes and endnotes, and a series of fixes in documents, tables and spreadsheets. They are still development releases.

ifcx.title: Save as IFCX
ifcx.desc: Documents, spreadsheets and presentations save and reopen as .ifcx, with the original Office document kept inside.

notes.title: Footnotes and endnotes
notes.desc: Convert notes, numbering that matches between reference and note, and PDF links in notes, tables, headers and footers.

sheet.title: Spreadsheet
sheet.desc: Extended name management, function help and formula colours while you type, and recalculated results that are also right in the saved XLSX file.

tables.title: Tables
tables.desc: Clear row and column actions, Tab navigation and a new last row. Splitting and merging keep the column widths.

ready.q: Is it ready for daily work?
ready.a: Not quite yet. The releases are development releases and not yet signed off for production work. Test with copies of your files and see the known limitations in the release audit on GitHub.

files.a: DOCX, XLSX and PPTX directly, CSV and TSV, Markdown, and MDB and ACCDB as an editable copy. Documents, spreadsheets and presentations also save and open .ifcx. For OpenDocument and older Office formats, install LibreOffice as well.

cost.a: Nothing. Open Office Studio is open source under the Apache-2.0 licence: no licence fees and no account.

privacy.a: On your own computer. There is no telemetry. Network connections are only for what you set up, such as your mail server. Passwords are kept in your operating system’s keychain.

apps.q: Do I have to install the whole suite?
apps.a: No. Documents, spreadsheet, presentation, email, notes and database also come as separate apps. The suite and a separate app each have their own profile; transfer notes with a backup.

access.a: No. Open Database Studio reads MDB and ACCDB itself and works in a SQLite copy; the original file is never written to. Access form designs and macros are inventoried, not executed.

tech.heading: Technology
tech.sub: For those who want to know how it is built.

tauri.title: Tauri 2 and Rust
tauri.desc: The desktop shell: files, conversion, email, windows and recovery.

react.title: React 19 and TypeScript
react.desc: The interface with ribbon, editors, charts and printing.

engines.title: Open document engines
engines.desc: The @betteroffice packages (Apache-2.0) for documents, spreadsheets and presentations.

sqlite.title: SQLite and its own VBA interpreter
sqlite.desc: For Access databases, with a DAO subset.

spell.title: Hunspell
spell.desc: Spell checking as WebAssembly, with dictionaries from pinned sources.

blueprint.title: OpenAEC house style
blueprint.desc: The same controls and look as the other OpenAEC apps.
